My sorghum plot is on our own land here in the North East, and I intercrop it as we always do — usually with cowpea to help the soil and feed the family. I will buy some urea if I can afford it at planting and top-dress, but fertilizer is costly and I cannot put as much as the extension people say. I keep my own sorghum seed from last harvest because the improved ones are expensive and not always available in the market, and I depend only on the rains — there is no irrigation here. My wife and grown children help me, but at weeding and harvest I will hire a few young men from the village to finish on time.
